newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: German's Kohl says euro will occur on schedule.
newsitem.headline: German's Kohl says euro will occur on schedule.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Monday Europe's single currency, the euro, would occur on schedule.
"The euro will come, will be brought about no matter what you may be reading and within the timeframe that we have agreed upon," Kohl told a news conference during an official visit to Australia.
European countries have set January 1, 1999, as the target date for the first phase of European Monetary Union with its single currency.
But there is deep division within the European Union and within member countries over the euro's introduction along with the imposition of strict fiscal and economic guidelines for euro countries.

Kohl's comment follows a similar reassurance by German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel, who said on Sunday the single currency must occur on schedule under strict adherence to economic stability criteria.
One of the key economic targets for countries to join the first phase of the monetary union is to reduce public budget deficits to 3.0 percent of gross domestic product this year.
